title: Adjacent transition square for the normalized coherent tensor tower
statement: For every scheme W, pair of cochain complexes P,Q and n, the prescribed level comparison at n+1 commutes with the quotient transition: the (n+1)-level comparison followed by the target transition equals the source transition followed by the n-level comparison.

source.place: Tags 0941 and 07A4, compatibility of the prescribed finite tensor comparison with consecutive quotient transitions

proof.text: For each degree, the quotient transition carries the unit of finite scalar extension at n+1 to the unit at n, by its normalized pure-tensor formula and preservation of 1. A completed-linear map between these restricted finite module sheaves is finite-linear after restricting the target along the quotient: the completion projection is locally surjective. Hence the scalar-extension adjunction detects equality after precomposition with its unit. The stipulated transpose equation for the reduction-evaluation isomorphism and the limit-cone identity then prove its adjacent transition square. Apply this degreewise to each input complex.

source.place: Tag 0941, the ringed sequence site and its limit cone; the unit normalization is that of the completed pullback tower core.

proof.text: Compose this square with the two inverse reduction-evaluation isomorphisms. The resulting equation says that the inverse evaluation comparison carries the actual horizontal section transition to the finite quotient transition. Transporting section types through restriction and evaluation uses exactly the underlying-section characterization of coefficientSequenceRestriction; no claim about lifting derived evaluation maps is involved.

source.place: Tag 0941, ordinary restriction and evaluation of the ringed sequence site.

proof.text: Evaluate the three defining factors of the level comparison on a homogeneous tensor generator: restriction/evaluation identifies the section, the normalized coefficientEvaluationTensorIso sends it to the tensor of the evaluated sections, and the total tensor of the two inverse reduction comparisons applies those inverses to the two factors. Naturality of the sheafification unit and of the direct-sum summand inclusion shows directly that restricting a total tensor generator restricts each factor. The module-sheafification unit and the underlying abelian-sheafification unit agree after forgetting the module action, so the coefficient-generator convention agrees with the prescribed finite tensor-generator convention.

source.place: Tag 07A4, ordinary total tensor construction, and Modules on Sites Tag 03EK, naturality of sheafified tensor generators.

proof.text: Precompose the desired square by the inverse level comparison at n+1. The locally surjective completion projection permits testing completed-linear maps out of the finite total tensor on homogeneous pure-tensor generators. Evaluation on sections is surjective, so choose sequence sections representing the images of the two finite sections under reduction evaluation. Step 3 identifies their inverse image under the level comparison. The source transition restricts each factor; step 2 identifies the resulting inverse-evaluation sections with the two finite quotient transitions. These are exactly the two factors in the prescribed target tensor-transition formula. Thus the two maps agree on every tensor summand in every degree, hence as cochain maps.

source.place: Tags 07A4 and 0941, generator computation of the ordinary tensor comparison and its quotient transitions.

lean.statement:
theorem pullbackTensorTensorTowerLevel_transition
    (W : Scheme.{u})
    (P Q : CochainComplex (integralTowerModules l E W) ℤ) (n : ℕ) :
    (pullbackTensorTensorTowerLevel l E W P Q (n + 1)).hom ≫
        ((integralOperationsTensorTowerFunctor l E W).obj (P,Q)).map
          (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op =
      (pullbackTensorRestrictedTower l E W
        ((coefficientTotalTensor.{u, u + 1, u}
          (coefficientSequenceTopology (ProEt.topology W))
          (coefficientSequenceCommRingSheaf l E W)).obj
          ((((pullbackTensorOrdinaryReduction l E W).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P),
            (((pullbackTensorOrdinaryReduction l E W).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj Q)))
        ).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op ≫
      (pullbackTensorTensorTowerLevel l E W P Q n).hom
